passages.text: You are to imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul follows Christ.
\r\nYou should imitate Paul.
\r\nPaul imitates Christ.
\r\nYou should imitate Paul as he imitates Christ.
passages.original: Μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε καθὼς κἀγὼ Χριστοῦ

passages.text: Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this message to the church in Corinth.
Paul commends the believers.
You remember me in everything.
You keep the traditions.
I passed these traditions on to you.
You maintain them as I gave them to you.
passages.original: Ἐπαινῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς ὅτι πάντα μου μέμνησθε καὶ καθὼς παρέδωκα ὑμῖν τὰς παραδόσεις κατέχετε

passages.text: But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul wants the believers to understand an important truth.
Christ is the head of every man.
The man is the head of the woman.
God is the head of Christ.
passages.original: Θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς εἰδέναι ὅτι παντὸς ἀνδρὸς ἡ κεφαλὴ ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν κεφαλὴ δὲ γυναικὸς ὁ ἀνήρ κεφαλὴ δὲ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὁ Θεός

passages.text: Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Corinthians.
Paul teaches about prayer and prophecy.
Paul says, "Every man who prays with his head covered dishonors his head."
Every man who prophesies with his head covered also dishonors his head.
passages.original: Πᾶς ἀνὴρ προσευχόμενος ἢ προφητεύων κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is just as if her head were shaved.
passages.sermon: Every woman who prays with her head uncovered dishonors her head.\r\nEvery woman who prophesies with her head uncovered also dishonors her head.\r\nA woman with an uncovered head is just like a woman whose head is shaved.
passages.original: πᾶσα δὲ γυνὴ προσευχομένη ἢ προφητεύουσα ἀκατακαλύπτῳ τῇ κεφαλῇ καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτῆς ἓν γάρ ἐστιν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ τῇ ἐξυρημένῃ

passages.text: If a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off. And if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head.
passages.sermon: A woman should cover her head when she prays or prophesies.\r\nIf a woman does not cover her head, she should have her hair cut off.\r\nIf it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off, she should cover her head.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ οὐ κατακαλύπτεται γυνή καὶ κειράσθω εἰ δὲ αἰσχρὸν γυναικὶ τὸ κείρασθαι ἢ ξυρᾶσθαι κατακαλυπτέσθω

passages.text: A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but the woman is the glory of man.
passages.sermon:
A man should not cover his head.
A man is the image of God.
A man is the glory of God.
A woman is the glory of man.
passages.original: Ἀνὴρ μὲν γὰρ οὐκ ὀφείλει κατακαλύπτεσθαι τὴν κεφαλήν εἰκὼν καὶ δόξα Θεοῦ ὑπάρχων ἡ γυνὴ δὲ δόξα ἀνδρός ἐστιν

passages.text: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.
passages.sermon: Man did not come from woman.\r\nWoman came from man.
passages.original: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἀνὴρ ἐκ γυναικός ἀλλὰ γυνὴ ἐξ ἀνδρός

passages.text: Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.
passages.sermon: God created man first.\r\nGod did not create man for the sake of woman.\r\nGod created woman for the sake of man.
passages.original: καὶ γὰρ οὐκ ἐκτίσθη ἀνὴρ διὰ τὴν γυναῖκα ἀλλὰ γυνὴ διὰ τὸν ἄνδρα

passages.text: For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.
passages.sermon: A woman should have a sign of authority on her head.\r\nShe should do this because of the angels.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο ὀφείλει ἡ γυνὴ ἐξουσίαν ἔχειν ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς διὰ τοὺς ἀγγέλους

passages.text: In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.
passages.sermon: In the Lord, woman is not independent of man.\r\nIn the Lord, man is not independent of woman.
passages.original: Πλὴν οὔτε γυνὴ χωρὶς ἀνδρὸς οὔτε ἀνὴρ χωρὶς γυναικὸς ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman. But everything comes from God.
passages.sermon: Woman came from man.\r\nMan is born of woman.\r\nGod is the source of everything.
passages.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνδρός οὕτως καὶ ὁ ἀνὴρ διὰ τῆς γυναικός τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
He addresses Christian men and women.
He asks a question about worship practices.
He says, "Judge for yourselves."
He asks, "Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?"
passages.original: Ἐν ὑμῖν αὐτοῖς κρίνατε πρέπον ἐστὶν γυναῖκα ἀκατακάλυπτον τῷ Θεῷ προσεύχεσθαι

passages.text: Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him, but that if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For long hair is given to her as a covering.
passages.sermon:
Nature teaches us important things.
Nature shows us differences between men and women.
If a man has long hair, it brings him shame.
If a woman has long hair, it brings her honor.
Long hair is given to a woman as a covering.
passages.original: οὐδὲ ἡ φύσις αὐτὴ διδάσκει ὑμᾶς ὅτι ἀνὴρ μὲν ἐὰν κομᾷ ἀτιμία αὐτῷ ἐστιν γυνὴ δὲ ἐὰν κομᾷ δόξα αὐτῇ ἐστιν ὅτι ἡ κόμη ἀντὶ περιβολαίου δέδοται αὐτῇ

passages.text: If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul addresses customs about prayer and head coverings.
If anyone wants to argue about this teaching, we do not have any other custom.
The churches of God also do not have any other custom.
passages.original: Εἰ δέ τις δοκεῖ φιλόνεικος εἶναι ἡμεῖς τοιαύτην συνήθειαν οὐκ ἔχομεν οὐδὲ αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul gives instructions to the church.
Paul does not praise the church.
Paul sees a problem in their gatherings.
Their gatherings do not make things better.
Their gatherings make things worse.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ παραγγέλλων οὐκ ἐπαινῶ ὅτι οὐκ εἰς τὸ κρεῖσσον ἀλλὰ εἰς τὸ ἧσσον συνέρχεσθε

passages.text: First of all, I hear that when you come together as a church, there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the church in Corinth.
Paul addresses the believers who gather as a church.
Paul says he hears reports about them.
Paul hears that there are divisions among them.
Paul believes some of these reports about divisions.
passages.original: πρῶτον μὲν γὰρ συνερχομένων ὑμῶν ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀκούω σχίσματα ἐν ὑμῖν ὑπάρχειν καὶ μέρος τι πιστεύω

passages.text: And indeed, there must be differences among you to show which of you are approved.
passages.sermon:
There must be differences among you.
These differences are necessary.
They show which people among you are approved.
Approved people become clear because of these differences.
passages.original: δεῖ γὰρ καὶ αἱρέσεις ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι ἵνα καὶ οἱ δόκιμοι φανεροὶ γένωνται ἐν ὑμῖν

passages.text: Now then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
He addresses the believers who gather together as a church.
He says, “When you come together in one place, you do not eat the Lord’s Supper.”
Your gathering is not truly for the Lord’s Supper.
You are not sharing the meal as Jesus commanded.
passages.original: Συνερχομένων οὖν ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ οὐκ ἔστιν κυριακὸν δεῖπνον φαγεῖν

passages.text: For as you eat, each of you goes ahead without sharing his meal. While one remains hungry, another gets drunk.
passages.sermon:
Each person eats his own meal first.
No one waits for others.
One person stays hungry.
Another person gets drunk.
passages.original: ἕκαστος γὰρ τὸ ἴδιον δεῖπνον προλαμβάνει ἐν τῷ φαγεῖν καὶ ὃς μὲν πεινᾷ ὃς δὲ μεθύει

passages.text: Don’t you have your own homes in which to eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? What can I say to you? Shall I praise you for this? No, I will not!
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
He addresses their behavior during gatherings.
He asks, “Don’t you have your own homes to eat and drink in?”
He questions their actions.
He says, “Or do you despise the church of God?”
He says, “You humiliate those who have nothing.”
He asks, “What can I say to you?”
He asks, “Should I praise you for this?”
He answers, “No, I will not praise you.”
passages.original: μὴ γὰρ οἰκίας οὐκ ἔχετε εἰς τὸ ἐσθίειν καὶ πίνειν ἢ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοῦ Θεοῦ καταφρονεῖτε καὶ καταισχύνετε τοὺς μὴ ἔχοντας τί εἴπω ὑμῖν ἐπαινέσω ὑμᾶς ἐν τούτῳ οὐκ ἐπαινῶ

passages.text: For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: The Lord Jesus, on the night He was betrayed, took bread, and when He had given thanks, He broke it and said, “This is My body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of Me.”
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to the church in Corinth.
Paul received a teaching directly from the Lord Jesus.
Paul also gave this teaching to the church.
The Lord Jesus acted on the night He was betrayed.
Jesus took bread that night.
Jesus gave thanks for the bread.
Jesus broke the bread.
Jesus said, “This is My body.”
Jesus said, “My body is for you.”
Jesus said, “Do this to remember Me.”
passages.original: Ἐγὼ γὰρ παρέλαβον ἀπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου ὃ καὶ παρέδωκα ὑμῖν ὅτι ὁ Κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ νυκτὶ ᾗ παρεδίδετο ἔλαβεν ἄρτον καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ εἶπεν Τοῦτό μού ἐστιν τὸ σῶμα τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν τοῦτο ποιεῖτε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν

passages.text: In the same way, after supper He took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Lord.
Jesus ate supper with His disciples on the night He was betrayed.
After supper, Jesus took a cup.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “This cup is the new covenant in My blood.”
Jesus told them, “Do this whenever you drink it.”
Jesus said, “Do this to remember Me.”
passages.original: ὡσαύτως καὶ τὸ ποτήριον μετὰ τὸ δειπνῆσαι λέγων Τοῦτο τὸ ποτήριον ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη ἐστὶν ἐν τῷ ἐμῷ αἵματι τοῦτο ποιεῖτε ὁσάκις ἐὰν πίνητε εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἀνάμνησιν

passages.text: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until He comes.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the church in Corinth.
He explains the meaning of the Lord’s Supper.
Whenever you eat this bread, you remember Jesus.
Whenever you drink this cup, you remember Jesus.
You proclaim the Lord’s death each time you do this.
You do this until Jesus comes again.
passages.original: ὁσάκις γὰρ ἐὰν ἐσθίητε τὸν ἄρτον τοῦτον καὶ τὸ ποτήριον πίνητε τὸν θάνατον τοῦ Κυρίου καταγγέλλετε ἄχρι οὗ ἔλθῃ

passages.text: Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
passages.sermon:
The Lord Jesus gave bread and a cup to His followers.
The bread and the cup represent His body and His blood.
He told His followers to eat the bread and drink the cup to remember Him.
Anyone who eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy way sins.
That person is guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
passages.original: Ὥστε ὃς ἂν ἐσθίῃ τὸν ἄρτον ἢ πίνῃ τὸ ποτήριον τοῦ Κυρίου ἀναξίως ἔνοχος ἔσται τοῦ σώματος καὶ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ Κυρίου

passages.text: Each one must examine himself before he eats of the bread and drinks of the cup.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to Christians about the Lord’s Supper.
Each person must examine himself.
He must do this before he eats the bread.
He must do this before he drinks the cup.
passages.original: δοκιμαζέτω δὲ ἄνθρωπος ἑαυτόν καὶ οὕτως ἐκ τοῦ ἄρτου ἐσθιέτω καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ποτηρίου πινέτω

passages.text: For anyone who eats and drinks without recognizing the body eats and drinks judgment on himself.
passages.sermon:
Paul is speaking to Christians in Corinth about the Lord’s Supper.
Anyone who eats the bread or drinks the cup must recognize the body of the Lord.
If a person eats and drinks without recognizing the body, he brings judgment on himself.
He eats judgment on himself.
He drinks judgment on himself.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων κρίμα ἑαυτῷ ἐσθίει καὶ πίνει μὴ διακρίνων τὸ σῶμα

passages.text: That is why many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
He explains the results of not recognizing the body of Christ during the Lord’s Supper.
Many people among you are weak.
Many people among you are sick.
A number of people among you have died.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν ὑμῖν πολλοὶ ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ἄρρωστοι καὶ κοιμῶνται ἱκανοί

passages.text: Now if we judged ourselves properly, we would not come under judgment.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
He teaches about the Lord’s Supper.
He warns the believers.
If we examine ourselves,
we will not come under judgment.
If we judge our own actions,
God will not judge us.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ ἑαυτοὺς διεκρίνομεν οὐκ ἂν ἐκρινόμεθα

passages.text: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world.
passages.sermon: The Lord judges us.\r\nHe disciplines us.\r\nHe does this so we will not be condemned with the world.
passages.original: κρινόμενοι δὲ ὑπὸ τοῦ Κυρίου παιδευόμεθα ἵνα μὴ σὺν τῷ κόσμῳ κατακριθῶμεν

passages.text: So, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
passages.sermon:
Paul speaks to the believers in Corinth.
He calls them brothers.
He gives them instructions about their gatherings.
He says, “When you come together to eat, wait for one another.”
passages.original: Ὥστε ἀδελφοί μου συνερχόμενοι εἰς τὸ φαγεῖν ἀλλήλους ἐκδέχεσθε

passages.text: If anyone is hungry, he should eat at home, so that when you come together it will not result in judgment. And when I come, I will give instructions about the remaining matters.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Corinth.
Paul gives instructions about their gatherings.
If anyone feels hungry, he should eat at home.
This prevents judgment when you gather together.
Paul will give instructions about other matters when he arrives.
passages.original: εἴ τις πεινᾷ ἐν οἴκῳ ἐσθιέτω ἵνα μὴ εἰς κρίμα συνέρχησθε Τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ ὡς ἂν ἔλθω διατάξομαι
